o1.biggest_strength: It builds the whole launch around the real signal: on-feet shift-worker creators, problem-first hooks, Spark Ads from the nurse and server posts, and a $38 90-day contribution target.
o1.biggest_mistake: The read on blended lift is a little too clean unless the holdout is used, and a few campaign rules like the learning bar are simplified.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the incrementality read into the main decision rule and clarify creator rights/fees for any new Spark content from the existing creators.

o2.biggest_strength: It gets the unit economics right, names the winning creative direction, includes setup steps, and gives the team a usable 30-day operating plan.
o2.biggest_mistake: It is a bit less precise on launch sequencing and scaling, especially opening a SCALE/Smart+ path by Day 8 and judging Day 30 partly on TikTok-claimed orders rather than making the cleaner store/survey/holdout read central.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the first week setup/test plan more concrete, keep scaling more controlled until store-side reads agree, and add more specific Maria/Tasha hooks from the supplied customer language.

reason: I would rather hand Output 1 to the team because it is more tightly built on our data, starts with the two proven licensed creator posts, gives clearer spend release rules, and ties the Day 30 decision more directly to contribution dollars. Output 2 is good, but slightly more generic and a little looser on attribution and early scaling.
